Ask for the width and length of a field in metres. Cast each input to a whole number with int() (this is called casting). Print the area and the perimeter. Turf comes in rolls covering {{a3 + 1}} m² – print how many rolls are needed (part rolls count), for example:
[[out:0]]
solution:
w = int(input("Width: "))
l = int(input("Length: "))
area = w * l
print("Area:", area)
print("Perimeter:", 2 * (w + l))
print("Rolls:", (area + {{a3}}) // {{a3 + 1}})
hints: Perimeter is 2 × (width + length) – brackets first!
area // {{a3 + 1}} rounds DOWN. Add {{a3}} first to round up.

title: Sprint speed
description: Ask for a distance in metres and a time in seconds. Cast each input to a whole number with int() (this is called casting). Print the speed in metres per second, rounded to 2 decimal places with round(), for example: [[out:0:0]]
solution:
d = int(input("Distance (m): "))
t = int(input("Time (s): "))
print("Speed:", round(d / t, 2), "m/s")
hints: Speed = distance ÷ time.
Use / (not //) and round(..., 2).

print("Percentage:", round(score / total * 100, 1))
print("Marks missed:", total - score)

Round to 1 place with round(..., 1).

title: Computer memory
description:

[[out:0]]

hints: 2 to the power n is 2 ** n.

[[out:0]]
solution:

print("Area:", round(3.14159 * r ** 2, 2))

hints: ** happens before *, so 3.14159 * r ** 2 squares only r.

title: Sharing a taxi
description:
Ask for a taxi fare in pence and the number of people. Cast each input to a whole number with int() (this is called casting). Everyone pays the same whole number of pence, rounded UP so the fare is covered. Print, for example:
[[out:0]]
solution:
fare = int(input("Fare (p): "))
people = int(input("People: "))
each = (fare + people - 1) // people
print("Each pays (p):", each)
print("Extra collected (p):", each * people - fare)
hints: fare // people rounds down.
Add people − 1 first to round up.
Extra = what was collected − the fare.

title: Until the bell
description: School ends at {{a1}}:{{a2}}. Cast each input to a whole number with int() (this is called casting). Ask for the time now as an hour and then minutes (24-hour clock, before {{a1}}:{{a2}}). Print how long is left, for example: [[out:0:0]]

m = int(input("Minutes: "))

print(left // 60, "h", left % 60, "min left")

title: Class register
description:
Ask for names until the user types stop, appending each name to a list (but not stop). Then print how many pupils there are, and each name with its number, starting at 1, for example:
Pupils: 2
[[out:0:1]]
[[out:0:2]]
solution:
names = []
name = input("Name (or stop): ")
while name != "stop":
    names.append(name)
    name = input("Name (or stop): ")
print("Pupils:", len(names))
for i in range(len(names)):
    print(i + 1, names[i])
hints: A while loop keeps asking until the name is stop; append() each name.
len(names) gives how many there are.
Loop over the indexes with range(len(names)), and print i + 1.

# Add the new player, then find and print the winner
solution:

Define make_code(name, year) that returns the first {{a0}} letters of the name in capitals, followed by the year, for example AVA2024. Ask for a name and a year, store the result, then print it and its length, for example:
[[out:0]]
solution:
def make_code(name, year):
    return name[0:{{a0}}].upper() + year

year = input("Year: ")
code = make_code(name, year)
print("Code:", code)
print("Length:", len(code))

title: Total and mean
description:
Define total(numbers) that adds up a list with a loop and returns the sum. Ask how many numbers (cast it), read each one (cast it) into a list, then print the total and the mean, using the returned total, for example:
[[out:0]]
solution:
def total(numbers):
    t = 0
    for n in numbers:
        t = t + n
    return t

how_many = int(input("How many? "))
nums = []
for i in range(how_many):
    nums.append(int(input("Number: ")))
sum_of = total(nums)
print("Total:", sum_of)
print("Mean:", sum_of / len(nums))
hints: The loop adds each item of the parameter numbers to t; return t after the loop.
Casting each input with int() stores numbers.
Store the returned total, then divide it by len(nums).
